name: B4a
description: Haplogroup B4a is a subclade of B4 and the direct ancestor of B4a1a, the 'Polynesian motif' — the defining mtDNA marker of Polynesian populations. B4a is found among Austronesian-speaking populations of Taiwan, the Philippines, Island Southeast Asia, and Polynesia. B4a1a (the Polynesian motif) underwent a dramatic demographic expansion approximately 3,000–3,500 years ago when Austronesian-speaking seafarers began their extraordinary colonization of Remote Oceania, eventually reaching as far as Hawaii, New Zealand, Rapa Nui (Easter Island), and Madagascar.
interestingFact: B4a1a, derived from B4a, is called the 'Polynesian motif' because it is found in essentially 100% of indigenous Polynesian populations — Hawaiians, Maori, Samoans, Tongans, Tahitians, and Rapa Nui people alike. Its near-total fixation in Polynesia reflects the extraordinary demographic bottleneck of the founding Polynesian population, whose entire female ancestry may trace back to a few dozen women who carried this haplogroup during the peopling of Remote Oceania.
references: Pierson et al. (2006) — Deciphering past human population movements in Oceania: provably optimal trees of 127 mtDNA genomes. Molecular Biology and Evolution 23(10), 1966–1975.
